statement: A standard die, whose opposite faces add up to 7, sits on a table with 1 on top and 2 on the face pointing towards you. You tip it over away from you three times in a row. Which number is on top now?

choices.misconception: I thought three tips bring the die all the way round, so the 1 comes back to the top.
I followed only the first tip, where the face pointing towards me rolls up to the top.
I thought the top number goes up by one with each tip, so 1 became 4.
I followed two tips, which puts the old bottom face on top, and forgot the third tip.

hints: Follow one tip at a time. Which face rises to the top?
When a die tips away from you, the face pointing towards you rolls up to the top. Only four faces take turns on top; use opposite faces adding to 7 to name the hidden ones.
The faces that come to the top in turn are the one towards you (2), then the bottom (6), then the far face, which is opposite 2, so 7 - 2 = 5.

solutions.reliable: Tipping away from you turns the die over its far bottom edge: the face towards you moves up to the top, the top moves to the far side, the far side moves to the bottom and the bottom comes round to face you. Only four faces take part: top 1, front 2, bottom 6 (opposite 1) and back 5 (opposite 2). After one tip 2 is on top, after two tips 6, after three tips 5. The transferable idea: when a die rolls in one direction only the four faces in that ring move, and opposite faces adding to 7 names the ones you cannot see.
solutions.elegant: Three quarter turns forward end in the same place as one quarter turn backward. Tipping the die once towards you would bring the far face to the top, and the far face is opposite 2, so it shows 5.

whyOnTest: Dice questions test tracking faces in your head, using opposite faces adding to 7 to name the faces you cannot see.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
